To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

occupant behavior is the main contributor to the discrepancies in energy consumption between buildings and the simulation results, and that the occupant-behaviors related electricity load patterns can be used as a reference for the energy simulation and energy efficiency policy.

(i) electricity consumption patterns of occupants in Shanghai are highly variable, (ii) occupant electricity-use behaviors are influenced by their socio-economic status and (iii) occupant electricity consumption is significantly affected by the weather and climate.

The occupant behavior related load patterns in Shanghai residences are highly diverse, with a large portion of the residents consuming low electricity and a small number of white-collar workers consuming high electricity.
